NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 28, 10:04 AM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 22.5 DraftKings points for $7,700, against Baltimore. Dak Prescott (20.8, $6,300) and Drake Maye (20.6, $6,500) are next.

Malik Willis returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.50 projected points per $1,000 at $4,900.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 28, 10:04 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 8

Josh Allen, BUF vs BAL ($7,700)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.5 DraftKings points at $7,700, the 4th-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.7 points clear of Dak Prescott. The model includes 6.7 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.92 projected points per $1,000, 17th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.5 points with a simulated floor of 8.4 and a ceiling of 40.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 3.5-point favorite at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 28.5 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Dak Prescott, DAL vs ARI ($6,300)

Dak Prescott projects 2nd at the position with 20.8 DraftKings points at $6,300. The salary works out to 3.29 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Prescott averaged 20.9 points with a simulated floor of 7.9 and a ceiling of 38.3, and he holds 14% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Dallas is a 6-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 30.25 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Value: Malik Willis, MIA vs NE ($4,900)

Malik Willis projects for 17.1 DraftKings points at $4,900, which works out to 3.50 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 21 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.9 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Willis averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.8 and a ceiling of 31.4, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7.5-point underdog at home against New England, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.
